prs.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
prs.author: MukundaKatta
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same root cause: MCPError-family exceptions break on pickle/unpickle. The default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but MCPError.__init__ sets self.args to (code, message, data), which mismatches subclass constructors like UrlElicitationRequiredError's (elicitations, message=None) signature — causing a TypeError on unpickle and/or lost payload data (issue #2431). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same root cause: MCPError-family exceptions break on pickle/unpickle. The default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but MCPError.__init__ sets self.args to (code, message, data), which mismatches subclass constructors like UrlElicitationRequiredError's (elicitations, message=None) signature — causing a TypeError on unpickle and/or lost payload data (issue #2431). prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2478 fixes the problem generically at the MCPError base class via a dispatch helper (_restore_mcp_error) that every subclass can use through from_error_data, while still special-casing UrlElicitationRequiredError to use from_error — the exact same special-case #2555 hardcodes into a one-off __reduce__ on that single subclass. #2478's fix therefore covers the whole MCPError hierarchy (any current or future subclass with a mismatched constructor signature), not just UrlElicitationRequiredError, and also flips the `data` property from `pragma: no cover` to tested, indicating broader test coverage of the general pickling path. #2555's change is a strict subset of this behavior scoped to one subclass, so it becomes redundant once #2478 lands.

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` checks each union member with `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` but never unwraps `Annotated`, so it still mis-fires (still calls json.loads) on `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` — the standard FastMCP idiom for a described optional string parameter — because `Annotated[str, ...]` doesn't equal plain `str` and fails the simple-type membership test. #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` specifically to strip `Annotated[...]` before the `str | None` check, so it fixes the bug for that common real-world pattern where #2032 leaves it unfixed. #2032 does cover a broader set of unions (e.g. `int | None`, `str | bool`) that #3056's narrower `_is_optional_str` doesn't touch, but that generality doesn't compensate for missing the Annotated-wrapped case central to the reported corruption bug.

members.author: newbiehwang

clusters.pick_reason: #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` checks each union member with `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` but never unwraps `Annotated`, so it still mis-fires (still calls json.loads) on `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` — the standard FastMCP idiom for a described optional string parameter — because `Annotated[str, ...]` doesn't equal plain `str` and fails the simple-type membership test. #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` specifically to strip `Annotated[...]` before the `str | None` check, so it fixes the bug for that common real-world pattern where #2032 leaves it unfixed. #2032 does cover a broader set of unions (e.g. `int | None`, `str | bool`) that #3056's narrower `_is_optional_str` doesn't touch, but that generality doesn't compensate for missing the Annotated-wrapped case central to the reported corruption bug.

clusters.pick_reason: #2478 fixes the problem generically at the MCPError base class via a dispatch helper (_restore_mcp_error) that every subclass can use through from_error_data, while still special-casing UrlElicitationRequiredError to use from_error — the exact same special-case #2555 hardcodes into a one-off __reduce__ on that single subclass. #2478's fix therefore covers the whole MCPError hierarchy (any current or future subclass with a mismatched constructor signature), not just UrlElicitationRequiredError, and also flips the `data` property from `pragma: no cover` to tested, indicating broader test coverage of the general pickling path. #2555's change is a strict subset of this behavior scoped to one subclass, so it becomes redundant once #2478 lands.

members.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same root cause: MCPError-family exceptions break on pickle/unpickle. The default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but MCPError.__init__ sets self.args to (code, message, data), which mismatches subclass constructors like UrlElicitationRequiredError's (elicitations, message=None) signature — causing a TypeError on unpickle and/or lost payload data (issue #2431).
